learn.title: Very big, very small
learn.body: Scientific notation writes huge or tiny numbers compactly as $a\times10^n$, where $1\le a<10$ and $n$ is a whole number. The exponent counts how far the decimal point moves.

learn.title: Write 45000
learn.body: Move the decimal point until one digit is in front.

learn.title: Write 0.0032
learn.body: Small numbers get a negative exponent.

learn.title: Multiplying
learn.body: Multiply the front numbers, and add the exponents. $(2\times10^3)(3\times10^4)=6\times10^7$. If the front number reaches 10 or more, adjust: $20\times10^5=2\times10^6$.
Big number means positive exponent. Number below 1 means negative exponent.

questions.explanation: A negative exponent moves the point left: 3 places gives $0.0032$.
The decimal point moves 4 places left to get 8.3.
The point moves 4 places right, so the exponent is $-4$.

questions.prompt: In $a\times10^n$, $a$ is at least 1 and less than \_\_
questions.explanation: This keeps the form standard: exactly one digit before the decimal point.

questions.prompt: Which is written in scientific notation?
questions.explanation: Only 3.5 is between 1 and 10. The others have $a$ outside that range.

questions.prompt: Write $(5\times10^3)(4\times10^2)$ as $a\times10^n$ with $1\le a<10$. What is $n$?
